subject: Biotechnology
title: Allergen-Free Foods
description: A quick, practical guide to Allergen-Free Foods.

hook.text: Peanut allergy affects 32 million Americans — what if you could remove the allergens from the peanut itself?

buildup.text: CRISPR targets Ara h 1, Ara h 2, and Ara h 3 — the three major peanut allergen proteins. Knock them all out.

discovery.text: Gluten-free wheat is in development — silencing the alpha-gliadin gene family could help celiac disease patients.

twist.text: Removing allergens must not ruin taste or texture — proteins serve structural roles that must be compensated.

climax.text: Hypoallergenic soybeans with reduced P34 protein already exist in research — moving toward field trials.

punchline.text: Delete the danger, keep the flavor — allergen-free crops could save lives.

quiz.question: What is the main challenge in creating allergen-free crops?
options: Allergens cannot be identified in plant genomes
Removing allergen proteins may alter the food's taste, texture, or nutritional value
CRISPR cannot target multiple genes in the same organism
